observations.observation: Google Search Central says its automated ranking systems are designed to prioritize helpful, reliable information created to benefit people, and its self-assessment asks whether content serves an intended audience and helps readers achieve their goal.
observations.claim: A content process should define the intended audience and user goal before drafting so usefulness can be assessed against the real reader rather than search-engine attraction alone.
observations.uncertainty: Google's guidance describes what its systems seek to reward; it does not establish that every audience-first process will produce higher traffic or a causal effect on rankings.

observations.observation: Nielsen Norman Group describes a user-need statement as an actionable problem statement capturing who the user is, what they need, and why the need matters, and recommends grounding it in qualitative research before generating solutions.
observations.claim: Explicitly stating the user, need, and goal before producing the solution helps keep work focused on the problem rather than prematurely locking onto an output.
observations.uncertainty: This is UX research guidance rather than a controlled study of editorial publishing outcomes; it supports the process principle but does not quantify its effect on content performance.
observations.notes: NN/G guidance emphasizes real user needs, research inputs, and a success benchmark.
